messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We're building backend for a helpdesk SaaS for businesses and their customers.
Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.
Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.
Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

Customers should also be able to email support and reply from their mail client. Add this with
Action Mailbox. Each business receives mail at its subdomain under `HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN`,
default `support.example.test`; Acme gets `acme@support.example.test`.

Use Action Mailbox's relay ingress at `/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails`, authenticated
with `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD`. In test, process incoming mail before the request completes
so a separate worker isn't needed.

Incoming mail should open a ticket with its subject and plain-text message.

Find the business from the recipients, including Cc. Ignore mail addressed to multiple businesses.
Reuse an existing customer, or create one and send a verification email so they can later use the portal.
Receiving email shouldn't verify their account.

When staff post a public reply to an email-origin ticket, email it to the requester. Give each
ticket a private reply address at the support domain, so the customer's next email returns to
the right conversation. Only the requester may reply by email. Replies reopen pending or solved
tickets; a new message to the plain support address opens a new ticket.

Deduplicate deliveries by Message-ID. Invalid deliveries must not block a later valid retry.
Ignore automated/list mail.

**Initial Assessment and Deep Dive Strategy**

Fantastic! 54 runs, 2004 assertions, and *zero* failures! That's a clean bill of health on the testing front. A great starting point. The speed of the run is also a positive sign; efficient execution is always something I look for.

Now, though, the real work begins. I can't be satisfied with just knowing *that* the code works. I need a comprehensive understanding of *how* it works. So, time to dive deep. The goal here is complete comprehension: every line, every pattern, the conventions, the data schemas, the configuration, the serialization strategies, the services, the models, the mailers, and the test helpers. require "securerandom"

class UserToken < ApplicationRecord
  EMAIL_VERIFICATION = "email_verification"
  PASSWORD_RESET = "password_reset"
  PURPOSES = [ EMAIL_VERIFICATION, PASSWORD_RESET ].freeze
  TTL = {
    EMAIL_VERIFICATION => 24.hours,
    PASSWORD_RESET => 2.hours
  }.freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :user

  validates :purpose, presence: true, inclusion: { in: PURPOSES }
  validates :token_digest, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :expires_at, presence: true

  scope :for_purpose, ->(purpose) { where(purpose: purpose) }
  scope :usable, -> { where(used_at: nil, revoked_at: nil).where("expires_at > ?", Time.current) }

  def self.digest(raw_token)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw_token)

  scope :active, -> { where(revoked_at: nil) }

  def self.digest(raw_token)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw_token)
  end

  def self.issue_for(user)
    raw_token = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
    session = create!(
      account: user.account,
      user: user,
      token_digest: digest(raw_token),
      last_used_at: Time.current
    )
    [ session, raw_token ]
  end

  def self.authenticate(account:, raw_token:)
    return nil unless account.present? && raw_token.is_a?(String) && raw_token.present?

    session = active.includes(:user).find_by(account_id: account.id, token_digest: digest(raw_token))
    return nil if session.nil? || session.user.suspended?

    session
  end

  def active?
    revoked_at.nil?
  end

  def revoke!
    update!(revoked_at: Time.current) if active?

  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze

  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requested_tickets
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true, inverse_of: :assigned_tickets
  has_many :comments, class_name: "TicketComment", dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :ticket

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(subject) { subject.to_s.strip }

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: { maximum: 255 }
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :priority, presence: true, inclusion: { in: PRIORITIES }
  validate :requester_belongs_to_account
  validate :assignee_must_be_active_staff_in_account, if: -> { assignee_id.present? && (new_record? || will_save_change_to_assignee_id?) }

  before_create :set_initial_public_updated_at
  before_update :update_public_updated_at_if_customer_visible

  scope :recently_active, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :public_recently_active, -> { order(public_updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :for_requester, ->(user) { where(requester_id: user.id) }
  scope :with_status, ->(status) { where(status: status) }
  scope :with_priority, ->(priority) { where(priority: priority) }
  scope :unassigned, -> { where(assignee_id: nil) }
  scope :assigned_to, ->(user_id) { where(assignee_id: user_id) }
  scope :requested_by, ->(user_id) { where(requester_id: user_id) }
  scope :search_text, ->(query) {
    return none if !query.is_a?(String) || query.include?("\x00") || !query.valid_encoding?

    pattern = "%#{sanitize_sql_like(query)}%"
    where(
      <<~SQL.squish,
        tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\\'
        OR EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM ticket_comments
          WHERE ticket_comments.ticket_id = tickets.id
            AND ticket_comments.account_id = tickets.account_id
            AND ticket_comments.public = TRUE
            AND ticket_comments.body ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\\'
        )
      SQL
      pattern: pattern
    )
  }

  def open?
    status == "open"
  end

  def pending?
    status == "pending"
  end

  def solved?
    status == "solved"
  end

  def normal_priority?
    priority == "normal"
  end

  def high_priority?
    priority == "high"
  end

  private

  def set_initial_public_updated_at
    now = updated_at || created_at || Time.current
    self.created_at ||= now
    self.updated_at ||= now
    self.public_updated_at ||= now
  end

  def update_public_updated_at_if_customer_visible
    if will_save_change_to_status? || will_save_change_to_subject?
      now = Time.current
      self.updated_at = now
      self.public_updated_at = now
    end
  end

  def requester_belongs_to_account
    return unless account_id.present? && requester.present?
    return if requester.account_id == account_id

    errors.add(:requester, "must belong to the same account")
  end

  def assignee_must_be_active_staff_in_account
    return unless account_id.present?

    if assignee.nil?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member in this account")
    elsif assignee.account_id != account_id
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must belong to the same account")
    elsif !assignee.staff?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be a staff member")
    elsif assignee.suspended?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member")
    end
  end

class User < ApplicationRecord
  ROLES = %w[admin agent customer].freeze
  STAFF_ROLES = %w[admin agent].freeze
  MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8

  has_secure_password

  belongs_to :account
  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :user_tokens, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :requested_tickets, class_name: "Ticket", foreign_key: :requester_id, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :requester
  has_many :assigned_tickets, class_name: "Ticket", foreign_key: :assignee_id, dependent: :nullify, inverse_of: :assignee
  has_many :ticket_comments, foreign_key: :author_id, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :author
  has_many :sent_invitations, class_name: "Invitation", foreign_key: :invited_by_id, dependent: :nullify, inverse_of: :invited_by

  normalizes :name, with: ->(name) { name.to_s.strip }
  normalizes :email, with: ->(email) { email.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true, length: { maximum: 255 }
  validates :email,
            presence: true,
            length: { maximum: 255 },
            format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP },
            uniqueness: { scope: :account_id, case_sensitive: false }
  validates :role, presence: true, inclusion: { in: ROLES }
  validates :password, length: { minimum: MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH }, if: -> { password.present? }
  validate :password_must_not_be_blank

  scope :by_id_asc, -> { order(id: :asc) }
  scope :active, -> { where(suspended_at: nil) }
  scope :suspended, -> { where.not(suspended_at: nil) }
  scope :staff, -> { where(role: STAFF_ROLES) }
  scope :admins, -> { where(role: "admin") }

  def verified?
    verified_at.present?
  end

  def suspended?
    suspended_at.present?
  end

  def active?
    !suspended?
  end

  def owner?
    id.present? && account.present? && account.owner_id == id
  end

  def admin?
    role == "admin"
  end

  def agent?
    role == "agent"
  end

  def staff?
    STAFF_ROLES.include?(role)
  end

  def customer?
    role == "customer"
  end

  def verify!
    update!(verified_at: Time.current) unless verified?
  end

  def revoke_all_sessions!
    now = Time.current
    sessions.active.update_all(revoked_at: now, updated_at: now)
  end

  def clear_ticket_assignments!(now: Time.current)
    assigned_tickets.update_all(assignee_id: nil, updated_at: now)
  end

  def revoke_tokens!(purpose:)
    now = Time.current
    user_tokens.where(purpose: purpose, used_at: nil, revoked_at: nil).update_all(revoked_at: now, updated_at: now)
  end

  def update_password_and_revoke_sessions!(new_password)
    transaction do
      if !new_password.is_a?(String) || new_password.blank?
        errors.add(:password, :blank)
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, self
      end

      self.password = new_password
      save!
      revoke_all_sessions!
      revoke_tokens!(purpose: UserToken::PASSWORD_RESET)
    end
  end

  private

  def password_must_not_be_blank
    return unless password.is_a?(String) && password.blank?

    errors.add(:password, :blank) unless errors.added?(:password, :blank)
  end
end

  DEFAULT_PAGE = 1

  def paginate_collection(scope, key:, &serializer)

    count = scope.except(:includes, :preload, :eager_load, :order).count
    total_pages = count.zero? ? 0 : (count.to_f / per_page).ceil
    offset = (page - 1) * per_page

  private

  def paginate_collection(scope, key:, &serializer)
    page, per_page = pagination_params
    count = scope.except(:includes, :preload, :eager_load, :order).count
    total_pages = count.zero? ? 0 : (count.to_f / per_page).ceil
    offset = (page - 1) * per_page

    records = if offset >= count
                []
              else
                scope.offset(offset).limit(per_page).to_a
              end

    next_page = page < total_pages ? page + 1 : nil
    previous_page = if page > 1 && total_pages.positive?
                      [ page - 1, total_pages ].min
                    end

    {
      key => records.map(&serializer),
      count: count,
      page: page,
      per_page: per_page,
      next_page: next_page,
      previous_page: previous_page
    }
  end

  def pagination_params
    page = parse_positive_integer(params[:page], default: DEFAULT_PAGE)
    per_page = parse_positive_integer(params[:per_page], default: DEFAULT_PER_PAGE)
    per_page = MAX_PER_PAGE if per_page > MAX_PER_PAGE
    [ page, per_page ]
  end

  def parse_positive_integer(raw, default:)
    return default if raw.blank?

    value = Integer(raw.to_s.strip, 10)
    value.positive? ? value : default
  rescue ArgumentError, TypeError
    default
  end

  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

      created_at: account.created_at.iso8601(3),
      updated_at: account.updated_at.iso8601(3)
    }
  end

  def serialize_portal(account)
    {
      name: account.name,
      subdomain: account.subdomain
    }
  end

  def serialize_user(user)
    {
      id: user.id,
      account_id: user.account_id,
      name: user.name,

      created_at: user.created_at.iso8601(3),

    }
  end

      name: user.name,
      email: user.email,
      role: user.role,

    }
  end

  def serialize_invitation(invitation, now: Time.current)

      role: invitation.role,
      status: invitation.status(now),

    class EmailVerificationsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_active_account!

      def create
        ev_params = require_hash_param(:email_verification).permit(:email)
        email = ev_params[:email].to_s.strip.downcase

        if email.blank?
          return render_error("Email is required", status: :unprocessable_content)
        end

        user = current_account.users.find_by(email: email)
        if user && !user.verified?
          _record, raw_token = UserToken.issue_for(user: user, purpose: UserToken::EMAIL_VERIFICATION)
          UserMailer.email_verification(user: user, token: raw_token).deliver_now
        end

        render json: { message: "If an unverified user matches that email, a verification link has been sent." }, status: :ok
      end

      def confirm
        ev_params = require_hash_param(:email_verification).permit(:token)
        token_record = UserToken.find_usable(
          account: current_account,
          purpose: UserToken::EMAIL_VERIFICATION,
          raw_token: ev_params[:token]
        )

        unless token_record
          return render_error("Invalid or expired verification token", status: :unprocessable_content)
        end

        user = nil
        confirmed = false

        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          token_record.lock!
          next unless token_record.usable?

          token_record.consume!
          user = token_record.user
          user.verify!
          confirmed = true
        end

        unless confirmed
          return render_error("Invalid or expired verification token", status: :unprocessable_content)
        end

        render json: { user: serialize_user(user.reload) }, status: :ok
      end
    end
  end
end

      before_action :require_authentication!, only: :destroy

      def create
        session_params = require_hash_param(:session).permit(:email, :password)
        email = session_params[:email].to_s.strip.downcase
        password = session_params[:password]

        if email.blank? || !password.is_a?(String) || password.blank?
          return render_error("Invalid email or password", status: :unauthorized)
        end

        user = current_account.users.authenticate_by(email: email, password: password)
        unless user
          return render_error("Invalid email or password", status: :unauthorized)
        end

        if user.suspended?
          return render_error("User account is suspended", status: :forbidden)
        end

        unless user.verified?
          return render_error("Email address must be verified before signing in", status: :forbidden)
        end

        if current_account.cancelled?
          if current_account.reactivation_expired?
            return render_error("Account cancellation period has expired", status: :forbidden)
          end

          unless user.owner?
            return render_error("Account is cancelled", status: :forbidden)
          end
        end

        session, raw_token = Session.issue_for(user)
        render json: {
          session: serialize_session(session, raw_token),
          user: serialize_user(user),
          account: serialize_account(current_account)
        }, status: :created
      end

      def destroy
        current_session.revoke!
        head :no_content
      end
    end
  end

    class SessionsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_authentication!, only: :destroy

      def create
        session_params = require_hash_param(:session).permit(:email, :password)
        email = session_params[:email].to_s.strip.downcase
        password = session_params[:password]

        if email.blank? || !password.is_a?(String) || password.blank?
          return render_error("Invalid email or password", status: :unauthorized)
        end

        user = current_account.users.authenticate_by(email: email, password: password)
        unless user
          return render_error("Invalid email or password", status: :unauthorized)
        end

        if user.suspended?
          return render_error("User account is suspended", status: :forbidden)
        end

        unless user.verified?
          return render_error("Email address must be verified before signing in", status: :forbidden)
        end

        if current_account.cancelled?
          if current_account.reactivation_expired?
            return render_error("Account cancellation period has expired", status: :forbidden)
          end

          unless user.owner?
            return render_error("Account is cancelled", status: :forbidden)
          end
        end

        session, raw_token = Session.issue_for(user)
        render json: {
          session: serialize_session(session, raw_token),
          user: serialize_user(user),
          account: serialize_account(current_account)
        }, status: :created
      end

      def destroy
        current_session.revoke!
        head :no_content
      end
    end

      skip_before_action :require_account!, only: :create
      before_action :require_authentication!, only: %i[show cancel reactivate]
      before_action :require_active_account!, only: %i[show cancel]
      before_action :require_owner!, only: %i[cancel reactivate]

      def create
        account_envelope = require_hash_param(:account)
        admin_envelope = require_hash_param(:admin, account_envelope)

        result = AccountSignup.new(
          account_params: account_envelope.permit(:name, :subdomain),
          admin_params: admin_envelope.permit(:name, :email, :password)
        ).call

        if result.success?
          render json: {

            user: serialize_user(result.user)
          }, status: :created
        else
          render_validation_errors(result.errors)
        end

      def show
        render json: { account: serialize_account(current_account) }, status: :ok
      end

      def cancel
        current_account.cancel!
        render json: { account: serialize_account(current_account.reload) }, status: :ok
      end

      def reactivate
        unless current_account.cancelled?
          return render_error("Account is not cancelled", status: :unprocessable_content)
        end

        if current_account.reactivation_expired?
          return render_error("Account cancellation period has expired", status: :forbidden)
        end

        current_account.reactivate!
        render json: { account: serialize_account(current_account.reload) }, status: :ok

    end

module Api
  module V1
    class BaseController < ApplicationController
      include ApiV1Serializers
      include ApiV1Pagination

      rescue_from ActionController::ParameterMissing do |e|
        render_error(e.message, status: :bad_request)
      end

      rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound, ActiveModel::RangeError do
        render_error("Not found", status: :not_found)
      end

      rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid do |e|
        render_model_errors(e.record)
      end

      before_action :require_account!

      private

      attr_reader :current_account, :current_session, :current_user

      def require_account!
        subdomain = request.headers["X-Helpdesk-Account"].to_s.strip.downcase
        if subdomain.blank?
          return render_error("X-Helpdesk-Account header is required", status: :bad_request)
        end

        @current_account = Account.find_by(subdomain: subdomain)
        unless @current_account
          render_error("Account not found", status: :not_found)
        end
      end

      def require_authentication!
        token = extract_bearer_token
        @current_session = Session.authenticate(account: current_account, raw_token: token)
        unless @current_session
          return render_error("Authentication required", status: :unauthorized)
        end

        @current_user = @current_session.user
      end

      def require_active_account!
        if current_account.cancelled?
          render_error("Account is cancelled", status: :forbidden)
        end
      end

      def require_owner!
        unless current_user&.owner?
          render_error("Only the account owner can perform this action", status: :forbidden)
        end
      end

      def require_admin!
        unless current_user&.admin?
          render_error("Admin access required", status: :forbidden)
        end
      end

      def require_staff!
        unless current_user&.staff?
          render_error("Staff access required", status: :forbidden)
        end
      end

      def require_hash_param(key, source = params)
        value = source.require(key)
        unless value.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
          raise ActionController::ParameterMissing.new(key)
        end

        value
      end

      def optional_hash_param(key, source = params)
        return nil unless source.key?(key)

        value = source[key]
        return nil if value.nil?

        unless value.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
          raise ActionController::ParameterMissing.new(key)
        end

        value
      end

      def parse_id_param(key = :id)
        raw = params[key]
        value = Integer(raw.to_s, 10)
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless value.positive?

        value
      rescue ArgumentError, TypeError
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
      end

      def extract_bearer_token
        header = request.headers["Authorization"].to_s
        scheme, token = header.split(/\s+/, 2)
        return nil unless scheme&.casecmp?("Bearer") && token.present?

        token.strip
      end

      def render_error(message, status:, errors: nil)
        payload = { error: message }
        payload[:errors] = errors if errors.present?
        render json: payload, status: status
      end

      def render_model_errors(record)
        errors_hash = record.errors.to_hash(true)
        message = record.errors.full_messages.first || "Validation failed"
        render_error(message, status: :unprocessable_content, errors: errors_hash)
      end

      def render_validation_errors(errors_hash)
        message = errors_hash.values.flatten.first || "Validation failed"
        render_error(message, status: :unprocessable_content, errors: errors_hash)
      end
    end
  end
end
"

module ActionMailbox
  # The base class for all Action Mailbox ingress controllers.
  class BaseController < ActionController::Base
    skip_forgery_protection

    before_action :ensure_configured

    private
      def ensure_configured
        unless ActionMailbox.ingress == ingress_name
          head :not_found
        end
      end

      def ingress_name
        self.class.name.remove(/\AActionMailbox::Ingresses::/, /::InboundEmailsController\z/).underscore.to_sym

        if password.present?

        else
          raise ArgumentError, "Missing required ingress credentials"
        end
      end

      def password

module ActionMailbox
  # Ingests inbound emails from Mailgun. Requires the following parameters:
  #
  # - +body-mime+: The full RFC 822 message

module ActionMailbox
  # Ingests inbound emails relayed from an SMTP server.
  #
  # Authenticates requests using HTTP basic access authentication. The username is always +actionmailbox+, and the
  # password is read from the application's encrypted credentials or an environment variable. See the Usage section below.
  #
  # Note that basic authentication is insecure over unencrypted HTTP. An attacker that intercepts cleartext requests to
  # the ingress can learn its password. You should only use this ingress over HTTPS.
  #
  # Returns:
  #
  # - <tt>204 No Content</tt> if an inbound email is successfully recorded and enqueued for routing to the appropriate mailbox
  # - <tt>401 Unauthorized</tt> if the request could not be authenticated
  # - <tt>404 Not Found</tt> if Action Mailbox is not configured to accept inbound emails relayed from an SMTP server
  # - <tt>415 Unsupported Media Type</tt> if the request does not contain an RFC 822 message
  # - <tt>500 Server Error</tt> if the ingress password is not configured, or if one of the Active Record database,
  #   the Active Storage service, or the Active Job backend is misconfigured or unavailable
  #
  # == Usage
  #
  # 1. Tell Action Mailbox to accept emails from an SMTP relay:
  #
  #        # config/environments/production.rb
  #        config.action_mailbox.ingress = :relay
  #
  # 2. Generate a strong password that Action Mailbox can use to authenticate requests to the ingress.
  #
  #    Use <tt>bin/rails credentials:edit</tt> to add the password to your application's encrypted credentials under
  #    +action_mailbox.ingress_password+, where Action Mailbox will automatically find it:
  #
  #        action_mailbox:
  #          ingress_password: ...
  #
  #    Alternatively, provide the password in the +RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD+ environment variable.
  #
  # 3. Configure your SMTP server to pipe inbound emails to the appropriate ingress command, providing the +URL+ of the
  #    relay ingress and the +INGRESS_PASSWORD+ you previously generated.
  #
  #    If your application lives at <tt>https://example.com</tt>, you would configure the Postfix SMTP server to pipe
  #    inbound emails to the following command:
  #
  #        $ bin/rails action_mailbox:ingress:postfix URL=https://example.com/rails/action_mailbox/postfix/inbound_emails INGRESS_PASSWORD=...
  #
  #    Built-in ingress commands are available for these popular SMTP servers:
  #
  #    - Exim (<tt>bin/rails action_mailbox:ingress:exim</tt>)
  #    - Postfix (<tt>bin/rails action_mailbox:ingress:postfix</tt>)
  #    - Qmail (<tt>bin/rails action_mailbox:ingress:qmail</tt>)

require "rails"

require "active_job"

module ActiveJob
  # = Active Job Railtie
  class Railtie < Rails::Railtie # :nodoc:
    config.active_job = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
    config.active_job.custom_serializers = []
    config.active_job.log_query_tags_around_perform = true

    initializer "active_job.deprecator", before: :load_environment_config do |app|
      app.deprecators[:active_job] = ActiveJob.deprecator
    end

    initializer "active_job.logger" do
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) { self.logger = ::Rails.logger }
    end

    initializer "active_job.custom_serializers" do |app|
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job_arguments) do
        custom_serializers = app.config.active_job.custom_serializers
        ActiveJob::Serializers.add_serializers custom_serializers
      end
    end

    initializer "active_job.enqueue_after_transaction_commit" do |app|
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record) do
          ActiveJob::Base.include EnqueueAfterTransactionCommit
        end
      end
    end

    initializer "active_job.action_controller_parameters" do |app|
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_controller) do
          ActiveJob::Serializers.add_serializers ActiveJob::Serializers::ActionControllerParametersSerializer
        end
      end
    end

    initializer "active_job.set_configs" do |app|
      options = app.config.active_job
      options.queue_adapter ||= (Rails.env.test? ? :test : :async)

      config.after_initialize do
        options.each do |k, v|
          k = "#{k}="
          if ActiveJob.respond_to?(k)
            ActiveJob.send(k, v)
          end
        end
      end

      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        # Configs used in other initializers
        options = options.except(
          :log_query_tags_around_perform,
          :custom_serializers,
          # This config can't be applied globally, so we need to remove otherwise it will be applied to `ActiveJob::Base`.
          :enqueue_after_transaction_commit
        )

        options.each do |k, v|
          k = "#{k}="
          if ActiveJob.respond_to?(k)
            ActiveJob.send(k, v)
          elsif respond_to? k
            send(k, v)
          end
        end
      end

      ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_dispatch_integration_test) do
        include ActiveJob::TestHelper
      end
    end

    initializer "active_job.set_reloader_hook" do |app|
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        ActiveJob::Callbacks.singleton_class.set_callback(:execute, :around, prepend: true) do |_, inner|
          app.reloader.wrap do
            inner.call
          end
        end
      end
    end

    initializer "active_job.query_log_tags" do |app|
      query_logs_tags_enabled = app.config.respond_to?(:active_record) &&

        ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record) do
          ActiveRecord::QueryLogs.taggings = ActiveRecord::QueryLogs.taggings.merge(
            job: ->(context) { context[:job].class.name if context[:job] }
          )
        end
      end
    end

    initializer "active_job.backtrace_cleaner" do
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        LogSubscriber.backtrace_cleaner = ::Rails.backtrace_cleaner
      end
    end
  end

**A Near Miss! Thank Goodness for Diligence!**

Wow, that was a close one! I'm so glad we dug into this. I was just looking at `ActiveJob::QueueAdapters::InlineAdapter#enqueue_at` and it hit me - that `NotImplementedError` is a potential landmine. The method explicitly raises an error if we try to enqueue a job with it, and it's pretty clear why.

Let's break down the scenario: we're working with `config.active_job.queue_adapter = :inline`. If an `InboundEmail` gets created, the `after_create_commit :route_later` callback kicks in, which then calls `ActionMailbox::RoutingJob.perform_later(self)`. That calls `enqueue(job)`, leading directly to the `inbound_email.route` method. The mailbox runs, the email gets `inbound_email.delivered!`, which, crucially, triggers the `after_update_commit :incinerate_later` callback. This calls `ActionMailbox::IncinerationJob.schedule(self)`, which schedules it with a 30-day delay, calling `enqueue_at`, and *BAM!* if incineration is enabled, we'd hit that `NotImplementedError`. It's a chain reaction perfectly set to blow up, and quickly!

But then I saw that bit in `active_job/railtie.rb`, specifically:

ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_dispatch_integration_test) do
  include ActiveJob::TestHelper
end

My spider sense is tingling – the integration tests might have some magic there. We need to check `ActiveJob::TestHelper` to see if it overrides the `queue_adapter` during `ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest`.

      included do
        class_attribute :_test_adapter, instance_accessor: false, instance_predicate: false
      end

      module ClassMethods

        def disable_test_adapter

        end

        def enable_test_adapter(test_adapter)

messages.thinking:
**Deep Dive into Action Mailbox and Deduplication**

Okay, so I've been really digging into how Action Mailbox works, especially with the test environment set up to use `:inline` adapter and `incinerate` set to false. My understanding is that when we hit the `/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails` endpoint in a test, the job is processed synchronously thanks to `:inline`. That's neat, but it highlights a critical point:  we need to be super careful about how we handle deduplication, *especially* with retries.

Here's the crux of it: Action Mailbox's default `create_and_extract_message_id!` *isn't quite* what we need. It uses a unique index on `message_id` AND `message_checksum` to catch duplicates. That is, if the *exact* same raw email (same Message-ID and same raw bytes) arrives, it's deduplicated, which is fine. The problem is what the prompt requires.  If a valid email arrives after a bounced delivery with the same `Message-ID` but *different* bytes, the default behavior will *not* deduplicate it, resulting in the creation of a second `InboundEmail` row and route.

So, here's what's going on:  We *must* deduplicate based on `Message-ID`, but only after the email has been *successfully processed*.  We can't rely on the current unique index on the `action_mailbox_inbound_emails` table. It's a key requirement: a *valid* retry of an *invalid* email should be accepted, but any subsequent *identical* delivery with the same `message_id` after a *valid* email, should be discarded.

So, here's the *real* thought process.  I've got this scenario in my head:

1.  **Invalid Delivery:** An email arrives. It's invalid (e.g., empty body, unpermitted sender, unpermitted recipient, account cancelled, etc.).  Action Mailbox will create an `InboundEmail` row with the `message_id` and the `message_checksum`. Because it's a test environment, the `route_later` enqueues synchronously.
2.  **Valid Retry:** A *valid* email arrives *later* with the *same* `Message-ID`.  Here, two scenarios:
    *   **Different Bytes:** The email is valid (fixed body, fixed sender, new valid recipient), and the `message_checksum` is different, so we need to create the new InboundEmail row so that we can process it, by not blocking it by a previous bounced delivery.
    *   **Identical Bytes:**  This could happen if, say, the business account was re-activated. `message_checksum` is the same, meaning this has already been received, and thus should be deduplicated so this case still works correctly.

Here's what I've figured out:

*   The key is to *not* consider an email processed until our mailbox app *successfully* records it as a ticket or a comment. That must be done in a database transaction.
*   We'll use a separate table (or a unique index on a table like `ticket_comments` or a dedicated column) that tracks processed `message_id` values.  We'll use a `processed_message_id` (or similar) table with a unique index, and create the ticket/comment **inside the same database transaction** that *also* updates this table with the `message_id`. That way, the retry will be rejected because our mailbox app already processed it.
*   The `action_mailbox_inbound_emails` index is ONLY used to stop exact duplicate email raw bytes coming into ActionMailbox.

Now, a critical point, from testing: We can't destroy the `inbound_email` if a delivery is rejected (bounced or failed), or we'll break tests that check the `inbound_email`.  The ideal solution is to keep an `action_mailbox_inbound_emails` row around for the *first* delivery, which might fail or get bounced. Subsequent identical-bytes retries will be silently handled by `create_and_extract_message_id!` returning `nil`, so they're deduplicated.

**Deep Dive on Email Handling: Address Formats, Edge Cases, and Design Implications**

Okay, so I'm diving deep into this email feature implementation. First off, I'm thrilled with the potential of leveraging `mail.recipients` and `mail.recipients_addresses`, because they give us such a rich set of recipient data. I see everything in there - `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, the originals, and even forwarded addresses! My immediate thought is to carefully analyze every aspect, especially `x_original_to_addresses`, because malformed addresses can be a parse error waiting to happen. It's smart to extract addresses with `Mail::AddressList` or rescue any parse errors.

Now, it's time to build a robust and complete design, one that takes into account every single prompt requirement and edge case with the existing codebase.

I'm starting with a sentence-by-sentence analysis of the prompt, really getting into the details.

### Requirement Analysis

First, the key to the prompt is the support domain and addressing format. The system is responsible for two address formats: the support domain config (which I'll implement in `HelpdeskConfig`), and a private reply address for each ticket. For that, it looks like this: `DEFAULT_SUPPORT_DOMAIN = "support.example.test"`, followed by a series of helper methods to resolve it.

Now, for the critical part – the private reply address. This has to be carefully designed! I'm thinking: What formats can a private reply address take? The constraints are clear: it MUST be on the support domain, and it MUST be private. Why? Because the format must be unguessable. `SecureRandom.hex(16)` and `SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(24)` come to mind, but email case-sensitivity is critical! Some clients lowercase the address. We MUST use lowercase hex to be lossless (and RFC-5321 compliant).

Now, local-part length is crucial! I need to ensure compliance with the RFC 5321 max length of 64 characters. Let's look at the Account subdomain format. The format `/\A[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?\z/` allows for a possible 63-character subdomain, and if the subdomain is too long and the reply token long, that could lead to an email with a local-part that exceeds 64 characters. Therefore, to make the code resilient, and to guarantee that the length of the email address remains valid, I will choose to format it as: `reply+<token>@support.example.test`. The plus sign guarantees that the reply address is not the plain support address. And the hex-token will always be lowercase! This simplifies the design a ton!

This design makes sure that all these conditions are addressed:

1.  "Each business receives mail at its subdomain under `HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN`, default `support.example.test`; Acme gets `acme@support.example.test`."
2.  "Find the business from the recipients, including Cc. Ignore mail addressed to multiple businesses."
3.  "When staff post a public reply to an email-origin ticket, email it to the requester. Give each ticket a private reply address at the support domain, so the customer's next email returns to the right conversation. Only the requester may reply by email. Replies reopen pending or solved tickets; a new message to the plain support address opens a new ticket."

I'm checking ALL consequences for this design, and how to detect it, to prevent the following:

*   Emails addressed to *multiple* businesses - which can then be ignored.
*   Emails that mix the ticket address with the normal support address - which MUST route as a ticket reply and NOT open a new ticket.
*   Emails with tampered tokens - which are to be ignored, and must never open a new ticket, nor route to another business.
*   Emails being sent to the normal support address only - which MUST open a new ticket, even if there are "Re:" or "In-Reply-To" headers.

class RequestsAndTicketsConversationTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @account_data = signup_and_verify!(name: "Acme", subdomain: "acme", admin_name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
    @account = Account.find_by!(subdomain: "acme")
    @owner_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password").dig("session", "token")

    @agent = @account.users.create!(
      name: "Morgan",
      email: "morgan@acme.test",
      password: "agent-password-1",
      role: "agent",
      verified_at: Time.current
    )
    @agent_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "morgan@acme.test", password: "agent-password-1").dig("session", "token")

    @customer_data = register_and_verify_customer!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Avery", email: "avery@example.test", password: "my-customer-password")
    @customer_id = @customer_data.dig("user", "id")
    @customer_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "avery@example.test", password: "my-customer-password").dig("session", "token")

    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
  end

  test "full portal conversation lifecycle between customer and staff with status transitions and no emails" do
    # 1. Customer opens a request
    assert_no_difference -> { ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size } do
      post "/api/v1/requests",
           params: {
             request: {
               subject: "Cannot download my receipt",
               comment: { body: "The download button does nothing." }
             }
           },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token),
           as: :json
    end
    assert_response :created
    req = json_body["request"]
    assert_kind_of Integer, req["id"]
    assert_equal "Cannot download my receipt", req["subject"]
    assert_equal "open", req["status"]
    assert_equal @customer_id, req["requester_id"]
    assert req["created_at"].present?
    assert req["updated_at"].present?
    assert_not req.key?("requester")

    ticket_id = req["id"]

    # 2. Customer lists own requests, opens it, and reads its initial comment
    get "/api/v1/requests", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 1, json_body["count"]
    assert_equal 1, json_body["page"]
    assert_equal 25, json_body["per_page"]
    assert_nil json_body["next_page"]
    assert_nil json_body["previous_page"]
    assert_equal [ ticket_id ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/requests/#{ticket_id}", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal ticket_id, json_body.dig("request", "id")
    assert_equal "open", json_body.dig("request", "status")

    get "/api/v1/requests/#{ticket_id}/comments", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 1, json_body["count"]
    first_comment = json_body["comments"].first
    assert_equal "The download button does nothing.", first_comment["body"]
    assert_equal true, first_comment["public"]
    assert_equal({ "id" => @customer_id, "name" => "Avery" }, first_comment["author"])
    assert first_comment["created_at"].present?

    # 3. Staff (owner and agent) list tickets, open one with requester info, and read comments
    get "/api/v1/tickets", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 1, json_body["count"]
    listed_ticket = json_body["tickets"].first
    assert_equal ticket_id, listed_ticket["id"]
    assert_equal "Cannot download my receipt", listed_ticket["subject"]
    assert_equal "open", listed_ticket["status"]
    assert_equal(
      { "id" => @customer_id, "name" => "Avery", "email" => "avery@example.test" },
      listed_ticket["requester"]
    )

    get "/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_id}", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @agent_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal(
      { "id" => @customer_id, "name" => "Avery", "email" => "avery@example.test" },
      json_body.dig("ticket", "requester")
    )

    get "/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_id}/comments", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @agent_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 1, json_body["count"]
    assert_equal "The download button does nothing.", json_body["comments"].first["body"]

    # 4. Owner answers and marks ticket pending
    assert_no_difference -> { ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size } do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_id}",
            params: {
              ticket: {
                comment: { body: "Please try again now." },
                status: "pending"
              }
            },
            headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token),
            as: :json
    end
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "pending", json_body.dig("ticket", "status")
    assert_equal "avery@example.test", json_body.dig("ticket", "re",
  "output_tail": "(account: "acme", token: @owner_token),
          as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "solved", json_body.dig("ticket", "status")

    # 10. Customer replies to solved request without marking solved -> reopens to open!
    patch "/api/v1/requests/#{ticket_id}",
          params: { request: { comment: { body: "Wait, the PDF is blank." } } },
          headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token),
          as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "open", json_body.dig("request", "status")

    # 11. Staff changes status to pending without adding a comment
    assert_no_difference "TicketComment.count" do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_id}",
            params: { ticket: { status: "pending" } },
            headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @agent_token),
            as: :json
    end
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "pending", json_body.dig("ticket", "status")

    # 12. Customer replies to pending request AND marks solved in the same update -> becomes solved!
    patch "/api/v1/requests/#{ticket_id}",
          params: {
            request: {
              comment: { body: "Never mind, cleared cache and it works!" },
              status: "solved"
            }
          },
          headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token),
          as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "solved", json_body.dig("request", "status")

    # 13. Customer replies to ALREADY solved request AND marks solved in same update -> stays solved!
    patch "/api/v1/requests/#{ticket_id}",
          params: {
            request: {
              comment: { body: "Thanks so much!" },
              status: "solved"
            }
          },
          headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token),
          as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "solved", json_body.dig("request", "status")

    # 14. Staff reopens solved ticket to open without comment, then customer marks solved without comment
    assert_no_difference "TicketComment.count" do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_id}",
            params: { ticket: { status: "open" } },
            headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token),
            as: :json
      assert_response :ok
      assert_equal "open", json_body.dig("ticket", "status")

      patch "/api/v1/requests/#{ticket_id}",
            params: { request: { status: "solved" } },
            headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token),
            as: :json
      assert_response :ok
      assert_equal "solved", json_body.dig("request", "status")
    end

    # 15. Verify all 10 comments appear oldest first on both /requests/:id/comments and /tickets/:id/comments
    expected_bodies = [
      "The download button does nothing.",
      "Please try again now.",
      "Let us know which browser you use too.",
      "Still nothing on Firefox.",
      "Investigating Firefox now.",
      "Fixed the Firefox download header.",
      "Closing notes added.",
      "Wait, the PDF is blank.",
      "Never mind, cleared cache and it works!",
      "Thanks so much!"
    ]

    get "/api/v1/requests/#{ticket_id}/comments", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 10, json_body["count"]
    assert_equal expected_bodies, json_body["comments"].map { |c| c["body"] }
    json_body["comments"].each do |comment|
      assert_equal true, comment["public"]
      assert_equal %w[id name], comment["author"].keys.sort
      assert comment["created_at"].present?

    get "/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_id}/comments", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 10, json_body["count"]
    assert_equal expected_bodies, json_body["comments"].map { |c| c["body"] }
    assert_equal [ "Avery", "Jo", "Morgan" ], json_body["comments"].first(3).map { |c| c.dig("author", "name") }

    # Zero emails sent throughout the entire conversation
    assert_equal 0, ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size
  end

  test "customer can also mark request solved via solved: true boolean flag" do
    post "/api/v1/requests",
         params: { request: { subject: "Quick question", comment: { body: "How do I export?" } } },
         headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token),

          as: :json

    patch "/api/v1/requests/#{id}",

          headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token),
          as: :json

    @account_data = signup_and_verify!(name: "Acme", subdomain: "acme", admin_name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
    @account = Account.find_by!(subdomain: "acme")

      role: "agent",

    @customer_id = @customer_data.dig("user", "id")
    @customer_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "avery@example.test", password: "my-customer-password").dig("session", "token")

    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
  end

  test "full portal conversation lifecycle between customer and staff with status transitions and no emails" do
    # 1. Customer opens a request
    assert_no_difference -> { ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size } do
      post "/api/v1/requests",
           params: {
             request: {
               subject: "Cannot download my receipt",
               comment: { body: "The download button does nothing." }
             }
           },
           headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token),
           as: :json
    end
    assert_response :created
    req = json_body["request"]
    assert_kind_of Integer, req["id"]
    assert_equal "Cannot download my receipt", req["subject"]
    assert_equal "open", req["status"]
    assert_equal @customer_id, req["requester_id"]
    assert req["created_at"].present?
    assert req["updated_at"].present?
    assert_not req.key?("requester")

    ticket_id = req["id"]

    # 2. Customer lists own requests, opens it, and reads its initial comment
    get "/api/v1/requests", headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 1, json_body["count"]

    assert_equal ticket_id, json_body.dig("request", "id")
    assert_equal "open", json_body.dig("request", "status")

    assert first_comment["created_at"].present?

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 1, json_body["count"]
    listed_ticket = json_body["tickets"].first
    assert_equal ticket_id, listed_ticket["id"]

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 1, json_body["count"]

            as: :json

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "pending", json_body.dig("ticket", "status")
    assert_equal "avery@example.test", json_body.dig("ticket", "re

    assert_equal 0, ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size

  test "customer can also mark request solved via solved: true boolean flag" do
    post "/api/v1/requests",
         params: { request: { subject: "Quick question", comment: { body: "How do I export?" } } },
         headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token),
         as: :json
    assert_response :created
    id = json_body.dig("request", "id")

    patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{id}",
          params: { ticket: { status: "pending" } },
          headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @owner_token),
          as: :json
    assert_response :ok

    patch "/api/v1/requests/#{id}",
          params: { request: { comment: { body: "Found it, thanks!" }, solved: true } },
          headers: json_headers(account: "acme", token: @customer_token),
          as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "solved", json_body.dig("request", "status")
  end
end

**Deep Dive into Email Implementation**

Okay, so I've been digging into this email setup, and some interesting patterns are emerging. First, I noticed how the `ApplicationMailer` sets the `mail.transport_encoding = "8bit"`. This makes perfect sense when considering the need to ensure the inclusion of URLs in the email body doesn't cause any issues with quoted-printable soft line breaks, as confirmed by that integration test. Consistent, nice.

Now, the `From` and `Reply-To` headers on the staff reply emails are the main focus. I'm considering several options: using the `HelpdeskConfig.support_address(@account)`, the `reply_address`, or the generic `HelpdeskConfig.mail_from`. The core idea is to ensure that replies from customers go back to the right ticket. The crucial question is how to test this. The private reply address, or *token* as some systems would call it, needs to be testable.

There are several things I'm looking at and testing:

*   **Testable `reply_address`**: A test could get the correct ticket token by reading `mail.reply_to&.first || mail.from&.first`.

*   **Mail Client Behavior**: When the user clicks reply, the email client will look at `Reply-To` or `From`, as per RFC 5322. `Reply-All` will include both. If the `From` is not the correct subdomain, a `Reply-All` from the user will send to the incorrect address. If `From` is correct, a reply will return to the ticket. If the `From` is the ticket's private address, only the ticket will be included in the conversation.

*   **Test Case Logic**: This allows us to establish a test case which verifies the correct return path for customer replies.
    1.  Test can read the `reply_addr` from `mail.reply_to&.first || mail.from&.first`.
    2.  `assert reply_addr.end_with?("@support.example.test")` to test the support domain.
    3.  Assert the test address is *not* the general support address.
    4.  Then, consider how tests might directly check either `mail.from` or `mail.reply_to` individually. This is important to determine which header the email client, as a default, will reply to.

*   **Possible Header Configurations**: Three possibilities for `From` and `Reply-To`:
    1.  `from: reply_address`, `reply_to: reply_address`
    2.  `from: HelpdeskConfig.support_address(@account)`, `reply_to: reply_address`
    3.  `from: HelpdeskConfig.mail_from`, `reply_to: reply_address`

    *   Configuration 1, if `mail.reply_to` and `mail.from` are both the `reply_address`, ensures all replies go to the right ticket. No downsides, and cleanest configuration.

*   **Header Specifics**: The `from` of the display name when used with the `Mail::Message` object requires that special characters be escaped. In Ruby `mail` gem, display names can be safely formatted using `Mail::Address` or just a properly quoted string. Setting both `from: reply_address` and `reply_to: reply_address` avoids display name parsing pitfalls, is super clean, and rock-solid.

*   **Subject Line**: Standard "Re:" prefix for replies to maintain email threading.

*   **Threading Headers**: Setting `In-Reply-To` and `References` to properly thread the conversations, but not setting `Auto-Submitted`, `Precedence: bulk` or `List-Id` to avoid automated mail filters.

*   **Email Body**: Plain text with the staff comment clearly included, without alteration.

*   **API Serialization**: Needs to be checked against existing tests. It should be confirmed whether the `reply_address` is included or a `channel`/`origin` indicator. This should be tested against `serialize_ticket` or `serialize_request` for the exact serialization keys.

module Api
  module V1
    class RequestsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_authentication!
      before_action :require_active_account!

      def index
        base_scope = customer_requests_scope.public_recently_active
        result = TicketFilter.new(scope: base_scope, params: params, mode: :customer).call
        return render_validation_errors(result.errors) unless result.success?

        payload = paginate_collection(result.scope, key: :requests) { |ticket| serialize_request(ticket) }
        render json: payload, status: :ok
      end

      def show
        ticket = find_request!
        render json: { request: serialize_request(ticket) }, status: :ok
      end

      def create
        request_envelope = require_hash_param(:request)
        comment_envelope = optional_hash_param(:comment, request_envelope)
        subject = request_envelope.permit(:subject)[:subject]
        comment_body = comment_envelope ? comment_envelope.permit(:body)[:body] : nil

        result = RequestCreation.new(
          account: current_account,
          requester: current_user,
          subject: subject,
          comment_body: comment_body
        ).call

        if result.success?
          render json: { request: serialize_request(result.ticket) }, status: :created
        else
          render_validation_errors(result.errors)
        end
      end

      def update
        ticket = find_request!
        request_envelope = require_hash_param(:request)
        comment_envelope = optional_hash_param(:comment, request_envelope)

        status_provided = request_envelope.key?(:status)
        status_value = status_provided ? request_envelope.permit(:status)[:status] : nil
        solved_provided = request_envelope.key?(:solved)
        solved_value = solved_provided ? request_envelope[:solved] : nil

        result = TicketUpdater.new(
          ticket: ticket,
          actor: current_user,
          mode: :customer,
          comment_provided: !comment_envelope.nil?,
          comment_body: comment_envelope ? comment_envelope.permit(:body)[:body] : nil,
          status_provided: status_provided,
          status: status_value,
          solved_provided: solved_provided,
          solved: solved_value
        ).call

        if result.success?
          render json: { request: serialize_request(result.ticket) }, status: :ok
        else
          render_validation_errors(result.errors)
        end
      end

      private

      def customer_requests_scope
        current_account.tickets.for_requester(current_user)
      end

      def find_request!
        customer_requests_scope.find(parse_id_param(:id))
      end
    end
  end
end

module Api
  module V1
    class PasswordResetsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_active_account!

      def create
        pr_params = require_hash_param(:password_reset).permit(:email)
        email = pr_params[:email].to_s.strip.downcase

        if email.blank?
          return render_error("Email is required", status: :unprocessable_content)
        end

        user = current_account.users.find_by(email: email)
        if user && !user.suspended?
          _record, raw_token = UserToken.issue_for(user: user, purpose: UserToken::PASSWORD_RESET)
          UserMailer.password_reset(user: user, token: raw_token).deliver_now
        end

        render json: { message: "If a user matches that email, a password reset link has been sent." }, status: :ok
      end

      def confirm
        pr_params = require_hash_param(:password_reset).permit(:token, :password)
        token_record = UserToken.find_usable(
          account: current_account,
          purpose: UserToken::PASSWORD_RESET,
          raw_token: pr_params[:token]
        )

        unless token_record
          return render_error("Invalid or expired password reset token", status: :unprocessable_content)
        end

        user = nil
        confirmed = false
        suspended = false

        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          token_record.lock!
          next unless token_record.usable?

          user = token_record.user
          if user.suspended?
            suspended = true
            next
          end

          token_record.consume!
          user.update_password_and_revoke_sessions!(pr_params[:password])
          confirmed = true
        end

        if suspended

module Api
  module V1
    class RequestsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_authentication!
      before_action :require_active_account!

      def index
        base_scope = customer_requests_scope.public_recently_active
        result = TicketFilter.new(scope: base_scope, params: params, mode: :customer).call
        return render_validation_errors(result.errors) unless result.success?

        payload = paginate_collection(result.scope, key: :requests) { |ticket| serialize_request(ticket) }
        render json: payload, status: :ok
      end

      def show
        ticket = find_request!
        render json: { request: serialize_request(ticket) }, status: :ok
      end

      def create
        request_envelope = require_hash_param(:request)
        comment_envelope = optional_hash_param(:comment, request_envelope)
        subject = request_envelope.permit(:subject)[:subject]
        comment_body = comment_envelope ? comment_envelope.permit(:body)[:body] : nil

        result = RequestCreation.new(
          account: current_account,
          requester: current_user,
          subject: subject,
          comment_body: comment_body
        ).call

        if result.success?
          render json: { request: serialize_request(result.ticket) }, status: :created
        else
          render_validation_errors(result.errors)
        end
      end

      def update
        ticket = find_request!
        request_envelope = require_hash_param(:request)
        comment_envelope = optional_hash_param(:comment, request_envelope)

        status_provided = request_envelope.key?(:status)
        status_value = status_provided ? request_envelope.permit(:status)[:status] : nil
        solved_provided = request_envelope.key?(:solved)
        solved_value = solved_provided ? request_envelope[:solved] : nil

        result = TicketUpdater.new(
          ticket: ticket,
          actor: current_user,
          mode: :customer,
          comment_provided: !comment_envelope.nil?,
          comment_body: comment_envelope ? comment_envelope.permit(:body)[:body] : nil,
          status_provided: status_provided,
          status: status_value,
          solved_provided: solved_provided,
          solved: solved_value
        ).call

        if result.success?
          render json: { request: serialize_request(result.ticket) }, status: :ok
        else
          render_validation_errors(result.errors)
        end
      end

      private

      def customer_requests_scope
        current_account.tickets.for_requester(current_user)
      end

      def find_request!
        customer_requests_scope.find(parse_id_param(:id))
      end
    end
  end
end

module Api
  module V1
    class PasswordResetsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_active_account!

      def create
        pr_params = require_hash_param(:password_reset).permit(:email)
        email = pr_params[:email].to_s.strip.downcase

        if email.blank?
          return render_error("Email is required", status: :unprocessable_content)
        end

        user = current_account.users.find_by(email: email)
        if user && !user.suspended?
          _record, raw_token = UserToken.issue_for(user: user, purpose: UserToken::PASSWORD_RESET)
          UserMailer.password_reset(user: user, token: raw_token).deliver_now
        end

        render json: { message: "If a user matches that email, a password reset link has been sent." }, status: :ok
      end

      def confirm
        pr_params = require_hash_param(:password_reset).permit(:token, :password)
        token_record = UserToken.find_usable(
          account: current_account,
          purpose: UserToken::PASSWORD_RESET,
          raw_token: pr_params[:token]
        )

        unless token_record
          return render_error("Invalid or expired password reset token", status: :unprocessable_content)
        end

        user = nil
        confirmed = false
        suspended = false

        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          token_record.lock!
          next unless token_record.usable?

          user = token_record.user
          if user.suspended?
            suspended = true
            next
          end

          token_record.consume!
          user.update_password_and_revoke_sessions!(pr_params[:password])
          confirmed = true
        end

        if suspended
          return render_error("User account is suspended", status: :forbidden)
        end

        unless confirmed
          return render_error("Invalid or expired password reset token", status: :unprocessable_content)
        end

        render json: { user: serialize_user(user.reload) }, status: :ok
      end
    end
  end
end

**Deep Dive into Email Processing and Deduplication**

Okay, let's break this down. My goal is to ensure robust and reliable email processing, especially around deduplication and handling invalid deliveries. I'm focusing on several key areas, each a potential edge case:

1.  **Resetting Passwords for Email-Created Users:** I need to make certain that users who are created via email (like through auto-creation when a customer sends an email to support) can seamlessly reset their passwords and gain portal access. This hinges on proper email verification. This requires verifying their email so they can log in via portal, which should automatically happen during the password reset and email confirmation flow.

2.  **Handling Suspended Users:** I need to ensure suspended users are *completely* locked out. This means they cannot sign in, request password resets, be assigned tickets, or access any API endpoints. Importantly, their emails should be rejected if they attempt to interact with the system (both for new tickets and replies), but such rejections should not cause issues with valid retries later. Their emails must be marked "bounced" with no database side effects.

3.  **Distinguishing Staff and Customer Emails:** We have a delicate balance between staff users who are also customers, and email interactions. If a staff member is the requester, then a staff member is permitted to email that account. For replies, I must prevent external staff or customers from replying to the reply address of a ticket unless they are the *actual* requester. This requires checking both staff *and* customer emails to correctly process a ticket or reply. If there is a pending staff invitation, the mail must be rejected to prevent an unwanted customer account from being created.

4.  **Handling Subject and Plain-Text Message Extraction:** Now, let's get into the heart of the matter – the email content itself. Here's a meticulous breakdown:

    *   **Subject Handling**: First, I need to ensure that the subject is consistently handled, normalized, and validated. This means stripping whitespace, and handling missing or blank subjects carefully to conform to RFC 5322. If there is no subject, a new ticket should be created and defaulted to `"(no subject)"`. The prompt says "Incoming mail should open a ticket with its subject and plain-text message". This applies to a new ticket, but not an existing reply.
    *   **Plain Text Message Handling**: This is about extracting the usable content. I need to handle all MIME types, including single-part (`text/plain`), multipart (`multipart/alternative`, `multipart/mixed`), and HTML-only emails. The aim is to prioritize the `text/plain` part if available, and if HTML-only, strip HTML, sanitize, and extract the text content. We must preserve line endings. We should not attempt to strip replies, since this could alter legitimate content (emails from real customers often contain lines that begin with `>`).

module HelpdeskConfig
  DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL = "http://localhost:3001"
  DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM = "support@example.test"
  DEFAULT_SUPPORT_DOMAIN = "support.example.test"

  module_function

  def frontend_url
    raw = ENV["HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL"].to_s.strip
    url = raw.empty? ? DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL : raw
    url.chomp("/")
  end

  def frontend_origin
    uri = URI.parse(frontend_url)
    return frontend_url unless uri.scheme && uri.host

    default_port = uri.scheme == "https" ? 443 : 80
    origin = "#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}"
    origin += ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port && uri.port != default_port
    origin
  rescue URI::InvalidURIError
    frontend_url
  end

  def mail_from
    raw = ENV["HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM"].to_s.strip
    raw.empty? ? DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM : raw
  end

  def support_domain
    raw = ENV["HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN"].to_s.strip.downcase
    raw.empty? ? DEFAULT_SUPPORT_DOMAIN : raw
  end

require "securerandom"

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze
  ORIGINS = %w[portal email].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requested_tickets
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true, inverse_of: :assigned_tickets
  has_many :comments, class_name: "TicketComment", dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :ticket

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(subject) { subject.to_s.strip }

  before_validation :ensure_reply_token, on: :create

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: { maximum: 255 }
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :priority, presence: true, inclusion: { in: PRIORITIES }
  validates :origin, presence: true, inclusion: { in: ORIGINS }
  validates :reply_token, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validate :requester_belongs_to_account
  validate :assignee_must_be_active_staff_in_account, if: -> { assignee_id.present? && (new_record? || will_save_change_to_assignee_id?) }

  before_create :set_initial_public_updated_at
  before_update :update_public_updated_at_if_customer_visible

  scope :recently_active, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :public_recently_active, -> { order(public_updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :for_requester, ->(user) { where(requester_id: user.id) }
  scope :with_status, ->(status) { where(status: status) }
  scope :with_priority, ->(priority) { where(priority: priority) }
  scope :unassigned, -> { where(assignee_id: nil) }
  scope :assigned_to, ->(user_id) { where(assignee_id: user_id) }
  scope :requested_by, ->(user_id) { where(requester_id: user_id) }
  scope :search_text, ->(query) {
    return none if !query.is_a?(String) || query.include?("\x00") || !query.valid_encoding?

    pattern = "%#{sanitize_sql_like(query)}%"
    where(
      <<~SQL.squish,
        tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\\'
        OR EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM ticket_comments
          WHERE ticket_comments.ticket_id = tickets.id
            AND ticket_comments.account_id = tickets.account_id
            AND ticket_comments.public = TRUE
            AND ticket_comments.body ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\\'
        )
      SQL
      pattern: pattern
    )
  }

  def open?
    status == "open"
  end

  def pending?
    status == "pending"
  end

  def solved?
    status == "solved"
  end

  def normal_priority?
    priority == "normal"
  end

  def high_priority?
    priority == "high"
  end

  def email_origin?
    origin == "email"
  end

  def reply_address
    HelpdeskConfig.ticket_reply_address(self)
  end

  private

  def ensure_reply_token
    self.reply_token ||= SecureRandom.hex(16)
  end

  def set_initial_public_updated_at
    now = updated_at || created_at || Time.current
    self.created_at ||= now
    self.updated_at ||= now
    self.public_updated_at ||= now
  end

  def update_public_updated_at_if_customer_visible
    if will_save_change_to_status? || will_save_change_to_subject?
      now = Time.current
      self.updated_at = now
      self.public_updated_at = now
    end
  end

  def requester_belongs_to_account
    return unless account_id.present? && requester.present?
    return if requester.account_id == account_id

    errors.add(:requester, "must belong to the same account")
  end

  def assignee_must_be_active_staff_in_account
    return unless account_id.present?

    if assignee.nil?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member in this account")
    elsif assignee.account_id != account_id
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must belong to the same account")
    elsif !assignee.staff?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be a staff member")
    elsif assignee.suspended?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member")
    end
  end
end

class TicketComment < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :ticket, inverse_of: :comments
  belongs_to :author, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :ticket_comments

    return unless account_id.present? && author.present?
    return if author.account_id == account_id

  end
end

class TicketMailer < ApplicationMailer
  def staff_reply(ticket:, comment:)
    @ticket = ticket
    @account = ticket.account
    @comment = comment
    @author = comment.author
    @requester = ticket.requester
    @reply_address = HelpdeskConfig.ticket_reply_address(@ticket)

    prior_message_ids = @ticket.comments
                               .where.not(email_message_id: nil)
                               .oldest_first
                               .pluck(:email_message_id)
                               .filter_map { |id| format_message_id(id) }

    if prior_message_ids.any?
      headers["In-Reply-To"] = prior_message_ids.last
      headers["References"] = prior_message_ids.join(" ")
    end

    mail(
      to: @requester.email,
      from: @reply_address,
      reply_to: @reply_address,
      subject: reply_subject(@ticket.subject)
    ) do |format|
      format.text
    end
  end

  private

  def reply_subject(subject)
    subject.match?(/\ARe:\s/i) ? subject : "Re: #{subject}"
  end

  def format_message_id(id)
    cleaned = id.to_s.strip.sub(/\A<+/, "").sub(/>+\z/, "")
    return nil unless cleaned.present? && /\A[^\s<>]+\z/.match?(cleaned)

    "<#{cleaned}>"
  end
end
EOF

class TicketUpdater
  MAX_BIGINT = (1 << 63) - 1
  Result = Struct.new(:success?, :ticket, :comment, :errors, keyword_init: true)

  def initialize(
    ticket:,
    actor:,
    mode:,
    comment_provided: false,
    comment_body: nil,
    comment_public: true,
    status_provided: false,
    status: nil,
    priority_provided: false,
    priority: nil,
    assignee_id_provided: false,
    assignee_id: nil,
    solved_provided: false,
    solved: nil
  )
    @ticket = ticket
    @actor = actor
    @mode = mode
    @comment_provided = comment_provided
    @comment_body = comment_body
    @comment_public = comment_public
    @status_provided = status_provided
    @status = status
    @priority_provided = priority_provided
    @priority = priority
    @assignee_id_provided = assignee_id_provided
    @assignee_id = assignee_id
    @solved_provided = solved_provided
    @solved = solved
  end

  def call
    errors = {}
    saved_comment = nil

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      @ticket.lock!
      @pending_comment = nil

      errors = validate_and_apply_changes
      if errors.any?
        raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
      end

      @ticket.save! if @ticket.changed?
      if @pending_comment
        @pending_comment.save!
        saved_comment = @pending_comment
      end
    end

    if errors.any?
      Result.new(success?: false, ticket: @ticket, comment: nil, errors: errors)
    else
      reloaded_ticket = @ticket.reload
      reloaded_comment = saved_comment&.reload

      if @mode == :staff && reloaded_comment&.public? && reloaded_ticket.email_origin?
        TicketMailer.staff_reply(ticket: reloaded_ticket, comment: reloaded_comment).deliver_now
      end

      Result.new(success?: true, ticket: reloaded_ticket, comment: reloaded_comment, errors: {})
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e
    Result.new(success?: false, ticket: @ticket, comment: nil, errors: e.record.errors.to_hash(true))
  end

  private

  def validate_and_apply_changes
    case @mode
    when :staff
      validate_and_apply_staff_changes
    when :customer
      validate_and_apply_customer_changes
    else
      raise ArgumentError, "Unknown update mode: #{@mode.inspect}"
    end
  end

  def validate_and_apply_staff_changes
    errors = {}

    unless @comment_provided || @status_provided || @priority_provided || @assignee_id_provided
      return { base: [ "Provide a comment, status, priority, or assignee_id to update" ] }
    end

    @ticket.status = @status if @status_provided
    @ticket.priority = @priority if @priority_provided

    if @assignee_id_provided
      if @assignee_id.nil?
        @ticket.assignee = nil
        @ticket.assignee_id = nil
      else
        parsed_id = parse_assignee_id(@assignee_id)
        if parsed_id.nil?
          (errors["assignee_id"] ||= []) << "Assignee must be an active staff member in this account"
        else
          assignee = @ticket.account.users.staff.active.find_by(id: parsed_id)
          if assignee
            @ticket.assignee = assignee
          else
            (errors["assignee_id"] ||= []) << "Assignee must be an active staff member in this account"
          end
        end
      end
    end

    if @comment_provided
      @pending_comment = TicketComment.new(
        account: @ticket.account,
        ticket: @ticket,
        author: @actor,
        body: @comment_body,
        public: @comment_public
      )
    end

    collect_errors(errors)
  end

  def validate_and_apply_customer_changes
    errors = {}

    if @solved_provided && @solved != true && @solved != false
      (errors["solved"] ||= []) << "Solved must be true or false"
    end

    mark_solved_via_flag = @solved_provided && @solved == true

    unless @comment_provided || @status_provided || mark_solved_via_flag
      return errors.any? ? errors : { base: [ "Provide a comment or mark the request as solved" ] }
    end

    if @status_provided
      if @status == "solved"
        @ticket.status = "solved"
      else
        (errors["status"] ||= []) << "Customers can only mark a request as solved"
      end
    elsif mark_solved_via_flag
      @ticket.status = "solved"
    elsif @comment_provided && (@ticket.pending? || @ticket.solved?)
      @ticket.status = "open"
    end

    if @comment_provided
      @pending_comment = TicketComment.new(
        account: @ticket.account,
        ticket: @ticket,
        author: @actor,
        body: @comment_body,
        public: true
      )
    end

    collect_errors(errors)
  end

  def parse_assignee_id(raw)
    value = case raw
            when Integer
              raw
            when String
              return nil unless /\A[1-9]\d*\z/.match?(raw)
              Integer(raw, 10)
            else
              return nil
            end
    return nil unless value.positive? && value <= MAX_BIGINT

    value
  end

  def collect_errors(errors = {})
    unless @ticket.valid?
      @ticket.errors.each do |error|
        next if error.attribute == :status && errors["status"].present?
        next if error.attribute == :assignee_id && errors["assignee_id"].present?

        (errors[error.attribute.to_s] ||= []) << error.full_message
      end
    end

    if @pending_comment && !@pending_comment.valid?
      @pending_comment.errors.each do |error|
        (errors["comment.#{error.attribute}"] ||= []) << error.full_message
      end
    end

    errors
  end
end
EOF

module InboundEmailMessageId
  module_function

  def extract(mail, fallback: nil)
    raw = extract_raw(mail) || fallback
    normalize(raw)
  end

  def normalize(value)
    return nil if value.nil?

    cleaned = value.to_s.dup
    unless cleaned.encoding == Encoding::UTF_8 && cleaned.valid_encoding?
      cleaned = cleaned.encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace)
    end
    cleaned = cleaned.delete("\x00").strip
    cleaned = cleaned.sub(/\A<+/, "").sub(/>+\z/, "").strip
    cleaned.presence
  rescue StandardError
    nil
  end

  def extract_raw(mail)
    return nil unless mail

    mail.message_id.presence || raw_header_value(mail)
  rescue StandardError
    raw_header_value(mail)
  end

  def raw_header_value(mail)
    field = Array(mail[:message_id]).last
    field&.value.to_s.strip.presence
  rescue StandardError
    nil
  end
end
