class InboundEmailFilter
  AUTOMATED_PRECEDENCE = %w[bulk junk list auto_reply auto-reply autoreply].freeze

  LIST_AND_LOOP_HEADERS = %w[
    list-id
    list-unsubscribe
    list-post
    list-subscribe
    list-help
    list-owner
    list-archive
    mailing-list
    x-mailing-list
    x-beenthere
    x-loop
  ].freeze

  AUTO_REPLY_HEADERS = %w[
    x-autoreply
    x-autorespond
    x-auto-reply
    x-auto-response
  ].freeze

  AUTOMATED_SENDER_LOCALS = %w[
    mailer-daemon
    postmaster
    noreply
    no-reply
    donotreply
    do-not-reply
    bounce
    bounces
    autoreply
    auto-reply
    autoresponder
  ].freeze

  def initialize(mail:, from_email: nil)
    @mail = mail
    @from_email = from_email
  end

  def ignore?
    auto_submitted? ||
      automated_precedence? ||
      list_or_loop_header? ||
      auto_reply_header? ||
      auto_response_suppress? ||
      failed_recipients_header? ||
      null_return_path? ||
      multipart_report? ||
      automated_sender?
  end

  private

  def auto_submitted?
    header_values("auto-submitted").any? do |value|
      primary = value.split(";").first.to_s.strip.downcase
      primary.present? && primary != "no"
    end
  end

  def automated_precedence?
    header_values("precedence").any? do |value|
      AUTOMATED_PRECEDENCE.include?(value.downcase)
    end
  end

  def list_or_loop_header?
    LIST_AND_LOOP_HEADERS.any? do |name|
      header_values(name).any?(&:present?)
    end
  end

  def auto_reply_header?
    AUTO_REPLY_HEADERS.any? do |name|
      header_values(name).any? do |value|
        normalized = value.downcase
        normalized.present? && !%w[no false 0].include?(normalized)
      end
    end
  end

  def auto_response_suppress?
    header_values("x-auto-response-suppress").any? do |value|
      tokens = value.downcase.split(/[,\s]+/).reject(&:empty?)
      (tokens & %w[all oof autoreply dr rn nrn]).any?
    end
  end

  def failed_recipients_header?
    header_values("x-failed-recipients").any?(&:present?)
  end

  def null_return_path?
    fields = Array(@mail[:return_path])
    return false if fields.empty?

    fields.any? do |field|
      field.value.to_s.delete("<>").strip.empty?
    end
  rescue StandardError
    false
  end

  def multipart_report?
    return true if @mail.mime_type.to_s.downcase == "multipart/report"

    @mail.all_parts.any? do |part|
      mime = part.mime_type.to_s.downcase
      mime == "message/delivery-status" || mime == "message/disposition-notification"
    end
  rescue StandardError
    false
  end

  def automated_sender?
    return false if @from_email.blank?

    local, domain = @from_email.split("@", 2)
    return false if local.blank? || domain.blank?
    return true if domain == HelpdeskConfig.support_domain

    base_local = local.split("+", 2).first
    AUTOMATED_SENDER_LOCALS.include?(base_local)
  end

  def header_values(name)
    Array(@mail.header[name]).map { |field| field.value.to_s.strip }
  rescue StandardError
    []
  end
end
EOF

class InboundEmailRecipientResolver
  Entry = Struct.new(:address, :subdomain, :token, :reply?, keyword_init: true)
  Result = Struct.new(:status, :account, :ticket, keyword_init: true) do
    def valid?
      status == :new_ticket || status == :reply
    end

    def new_ticket?
      status == :new_ticket
    end

    def reply?
      status == :reply
    end
  end

  STRUCTURED_HEADERS = %i[to cc bcc].freeze
  EXTRA_RECIPIENT_HEADERS = %w[x-original-to x-forwarded-to delivered-to].freeze

  def initialize(mail:)
    @mail = mail
  end

  def call
    support_domain = HelpdeskConfig.support_domain
    entries = extract_support_entries(support_domain)
    return invalid if entries.empty?

    subdomains = entries.map(&:subdomain).uniq
    return invalid unless subdomains.size == 1

    subdomain = subdomains.first
    return invalid unless Account::SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT.match?(subdomain)

    account = Account.find_by(subdomain: subdomain)
    return invalid if account.nil? || account.cancelled?

    reply_entries = entries.select(&:reply?)
    if reply_entries.any?
      tokens = reply_entries.map(&:token).uniq
      return invalid unless tokens.size == 1

      token = tokens.first
      return invalid if token.blank?

      ticket = account.tickets.find_by(reply_token: token)
      return invalid if ticket.nil?

      Result.new(status: :reply, account: account, ticket: ticket)
    else
      Result.new(status: :new_ticket, account: account, ticket: nil)
    end
  end

  private

  def invalid
    Result.new(status: :invalid)
  end

  def extract_support_entries(support_domain)
    addresses = collect_recipient_addresses
    addresses.uniq.filter_map do |address|
      local, domain = address.split("@", 2)
      next unless local.present? && domain == support_domain

      has_plus = local.include?("+")
      subdomain, token = local.split("+", 2)
      Entry.new(
        address: address,
        subdomain: subdomain.to_s,
        token: has_plus ? token.to_s : nil,
        reply?: has_plus
      )
    end
  end

  def collect_recipient_addresses
    addresses = []

    STRUCTURED_HEADERS.each do |header_name|
      addresses.concat(extract_structured_header_addresses(header_name))
    end

    EXTRA_RECIPIENT_HEADERS.each do |header_name|
      Array(@mail.header[header_name]).each do |field|
        addresses.concat(parse_address_list_string(field.value.to_s))
      end
    end

    addresses.filter_map do |addr|
      cleaned = addr.to_s.strip.downcase
      cleaned if cleaned.include?("@") && !cleaned.include?("\x00")
    end
  rescue StandardError
    []
  end

  def extract_structured_header_addresses(header_name)
    fields = Array(@mail[header_name])
    return [] if fields.empty?

    results = []
    fields.each do |field|
      if field.respond_to?(:element) && field.element.respond_to?(:addresses)
        results.concat(field.element.addresses.filter_map(&:address))
      else
        results.concat(parse_address_list_string(field.value.to_s))
      end
    rescue StandardError
      results.concat(parse_address_list_string(field.value.to_s))
    end
    results
  end

  def parse_address_list_string(raw)
    return [] if raw.blank?

    Mail::AddressList.new(raw).addresses.filter_map(&:address)
  rescue Mail::Field::ParseError, StandardError
    raw.scan(/[A-Z0-9._%+\-]+@[A-Z0-9.\-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}/i)
  end
end

require "nokogiri"
require "uri"

class InboundEmailContentExtractor
  Sender = Struct.new(:email, :name, keyword_init: true)
  DEFAULT_SUBJECT = "(no subject)"
  MAX_SUBJECT_LENGTH = 255
  MAX_NAME_LENGTH = 255

  def initialize(mail:)
    @mail = mail
  end

  def sender
    @sender ||= extract_sender
  end

  def subject
    raw = sanitize_text(@mail.subject)
    cleaned = raw.gsub(/[\r\n]+/, " ").strip
    return DEFAULT_SUBJECT if cleaned.blank?

    cleaned.slice(0, MAX_SUBJECT_LENGTH).strip.presence || DEFAULT_SUBJECT
  rescue StandardError
    DEFAULT_SUBJECT
  end

  def plain_text_body
    text = if @mail.multipart?
             extract_multipart_body(@mail)
           else
             extract_singlepart_body(@mail)
           end
    normalize_body(text)
  rescue StandardError
    nil
  end

  private

  def extract_sender
    addresses = extract_from_addresses
    return nil if addresses.empty?

    address_obj = addresses.first
    email = sanitize_text(address_obj.address).strip.downcase
    return nil unless email.present? && email.length <= 255 && URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP.match?(email)

    raw_name = address_obj.display_name.presence || address_obj.name.presence
    cleaned_name = sanitize_text(raw_name).gsub(/[\r\n]+/, " ").strip
    fallback_name = email.split("@", 2).first.presence || email
    name = (cleaned_name.presence || fallback_name).slice(0, MAX_NAME_LENGTH).strip
    name = fallback_name.slice(0, MAX_NAME_LENGTH) if name.blank?

    Sender.new(email: email, name: name)
  rescue StandardError
    nil
  end

  def extract_from_addresses
    fields = Array(@mail[:from])
    return [] if fields.empty?

    results = []
    fields.each do |field|
      if field.respond_to?(:element) && field.element.respond_to?(:addresses)
        results.concat(field.element.addresses)
      else
        results.concat(Mail::AddressList.new(field.value.to_s).addresses)
      end
    rescue StandardError
      next
    end
    results
  end

  def extract_multipart_body(container)
    plain_parts = []
    html_parts = []
    collect_candidate_parts(container, plain_parts, html_parts)

    plain_parts.each do |part|
      candidate = normalize_body(decode_part_to_utf8(part))
      return candidate if candidate.present?
    end

    html_parts.each do |part|
      candidate = normalize_body(html_to_plain_text(decode_part_to_utf8(part)))
      return candidate if candidate.present?
    end

    nil

  def collect_candidate_parts(container, plain_parts, html_parts)
    container.parts.each do |part|
      next if part.attachment?

      if part.multipart?
        collect_candidate_parts(part, plain_parts, html_parts)
      else
        mime = part.mime_type.to_s.downcase
        if mime.blank? || mime == "text/plain"
          plain_parts << part
        elsif mime == "text/html"
          html_parts << part
        end
      end
    end
  end

  def extract_singlepart_body(part)
    return nil if part.attachment?

    mime = part.mime_type.to_s.downcase
    if mime.blank? || mime == "text/plain"
      decode_part_to_utf8(part)
    elsif mime == "text/html"
      html_to_plain_text(decode_part_to_utf8(part))

  def decode_part_to_utf8(part)
    raw = part.body.decoded

    text = raw.dup
    charset = part.charset.to_s.strip
    encoding = if charset.present?

    text.force_encoding(encoding)
    if encoding == Encoding::UTF_8

    else
      text.encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace)
    end
  rescue Encoding::ConverterNotFoundError, Encoding::InvalidByteSequenceError, Encoding::UndefinedConversionError
    raw.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8).encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace)
  end

  def html_to_plain_text(html)
    return "" if html.blank?

    doc = Nokogiri::HTML(html)
    root = doc.at("body") || doc
    root.css("script, style, head, noscript").remove
    root.css("br").each { |br| br.replace("\n") }
    root.css("p, div, li, tr, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, blockquote, pre").each do |node|
      node.add_next_sibling("\n")
    end

    root.text
        .gsub(/\r\n?/, "\n")
        .gsub(/[ \t]+\n/, "\n")
        .gsub(/\n{3,}/, "\n\n")
  end

  def normalize_body(text)
    return nil if text.nil?

    cleaned = sanitize_text(text).gsub(/\r\n?/, "\n").strip
    cleaned.presence
  end

  def sanitize_text(value)
    return "" if value.nil?

    str = value.to_s.dup
    unless str.encoding == Encoding::UTF_8 && str.valid_encoding?
      str = str.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8).encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace)
    end
    str.delete("\x00")
  end
end

cat <<'EOF' > app/services/inbound_email_processor.rb
require "securerandom"

class InboundEmailProcessor
  Result = Struct.new(:status, :ticket, :comment, keyword_init: true) do
    def accepted?
      status == :accepted
    end

    def duplicate?
      status == :duplicate
    end

    def rejected?
      status == :rejected
    end
  end

  def initialize(inbound_email:)
    @inbound_email = inbound_email
  end

  def call
    mail = parse_mail
    return rejected unless mail

    extractor = InboundEmailContentExtractor.new(mail: mail)
    sender = extractor.sender

    return rejected if InboundEmailFilter.new(mail: mail, from_email: sender&.email).ignore?

    resolution = InboundEmailRecipientResolver.new(mail: mail).call
    return rejected unless resolution.valid?
    return rejected unless sender

    if resolution.reply?
      requester = resolution.ticket.requester
      return rejected if requester.nil? || requester.suspended? || requester.email != sender.email
    end

    body = extractor.plain_text_body
    return rejected if body.blank?

    message_id = InboundEmailMessageId.extract(mail, fallback: @inbound_email.message_id)
    return rejected if message_id.blank?

    return duplicate if TicketComment.exists?(email_message_id: message_id)

    if resolution.reply?
      append_reply(
        account: resolution.account,
        ticket: resolution.ticket,
        sender: sender,
        body: body,
        message_id: message_id
      )
    else
      create_new_ticket(
        account: resolution.account,
        sender: sender,
        subject: extractor.subject,
        body: body,
        message_id: message_id
      )
    end
  end

  private

  def parse_mail
    @inbound_email.mail
  rescue StandardError
    nil
  end

  def rejected
    Result.new(status: :rejected)
  end

  def duplicate
    Result.new(status: :duplicate)
  end

  def create_new_ticket(account:, sender:, subject:, body:, message_id:)
    verification_token = nil
    created_user = nil
    ticket = nil
    comment = nil
    outcome = nil

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      account.lock!
      if account.cancelled?
        outcome = :rejected
        raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
      end

      if TicketComment.exists?(email_message_id: message_id)
        outcome = :duplicate
        raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
      end

      user = account.users.find_by(email: sender.email)
      if user
        if user.suspended?
          outcome = :rejected
          raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
        end
      else
        if account.invitations.pending(Time.current).exists?(email: sender.email)
          outcome = :rejected
          raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
        end

        user = account.users.create!(
          name: sender.name,
          email: sender.email,
          password: SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32),
          role: "customer",
          verified_at: nil
        )
        _token_record, verification_token = UserToken.issue_for(
          user: user,
          purpose: UserToken::EMAIL_VERIFICATION
        )
        created_user = user
      end

      ticket = account.tickets.create!(
        requester: user,
        subject: subject,
        status: "open",
        origin: "email"
      )
      comment = ticket.comments.create!(
        account: account,
        author: user,
        body: body,
        public: true,
        email_message_id: message_id
      )
      outcome = :accepted
    end

    if outcome == :accepted && created_user && verification_token.present?
      UserMailer.email_verification(user: created_user, token: verification_token).deliver_now
    end

    Result.new(status: outcome || :rejected, ticket: ticket, comment: comment)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    TicketComment.exists?(email_message_id: message_id) ? duplicate : rejected
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
    rejected
  end

  def append_reply(account:, ticket:, sender:, body:, message_id:)
    comment = nil
    outcome = nil

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      ticket.lock!
      account.reload
      requester = ticket.requester.reload

      if account.cancelled? || requester.suspended? || requester.email != sender.email
        outcome = :rejected
        raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
      end

      if TicketComment.exists?(email_message_id: message_id)
        outcome = :duplicate
        raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
      end

      if ticket.pending? || ticket.solved?
        ticket.update!(status: "open")
      end

      comment = ticket.comments.create!(
        account: account,
        author: requester,
        body: body,
        public: true,
        email_message_id: message_id
      )
      outcome = :accepted
    end

    Result.new(status: outcome || :rejected, ticket: ticket, comment: comment)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    TicketComment.exists?(email_message_id: message_id) ? duplicate : rejected
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
    rejected
  end
end
EOF

module ActionMailboxRetryableInvalidDeliveries
  def create_and_extract_message_id!(source, **options)
    raw_source = source.to_s
    message_checksum = OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(raw_source)
    message_id = extract_message_id(raw_source) || generate_missing_message_id(message_checksum)

    existing = find_by(message_id: message_id, message_checksum: message_checksum)
    if existing
      return retry_if_invalid_delivery(existing, raw_source, **options)
    end

    super(raw_source, **options)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    existing = find_by(message_id: message_id, message_checksum: message_checksum)
    existing ? retry_if_invalid_delivery(existing, raw_source, **options) : nil
  end

  private

  def retry_if_invalid_delivery(existing, raw_source, **options)
    return nil unless existing.bounced? || existing.failed?

    parsed_mail = begin
      Mail.from_source(raw_source)
    rescue StandardError
      nil
    end
    normalized_id = InboundEmailMessageId.extract(parsed_mail, fallback: existing.message_id)
    return nil if normalized_id.present? && TicketComment.exists?(email_message_id: normalized_id)

    target_status = options[:status]
    if target_status.present? && target_status.to_sym != :pending
      existing.update!(status: target_status)
    else
      existing.update!(status: :pending)
      existing.route_later
    end
    existing
  end
end

Rails.application.config.to_prepare do
  unless ActionMailbox::InboundEmail.singleton_class.ancestors.include?(ActionMailboxRetryableInvalidDeliveries)
    ActionMailbox::InboundEmail.singleton_class.prepend(ActionMailboxRetryableInvalidDeliveries)
  end
end

Importantly, we have to make sure that a failed authorization or media type validation *doesn't* block a later, valid email with the same `Message-ID`.

Next, we'll scrutinize how new and existing customers interact with ticket creation via email. We'll meticulously test email submissions from new customers, ensuring proper ticket creation with the right subject, status, origin, and an initial public comment. We'll verify that new users are created correctly, with email verification sent and that the customer cannot access the portal until after verification, even if they try password reset, and then that they can after. We'll cover the creation of tickets by verified and unverified existing users. We'll also deal with emails that have missing display names or subjects, creating fallback defaults. It's crucial to confirm correct handling of multipart emails, with extraction of the `text/plain` portion and ignoring any HTML or attachments. We need to confirm that email encoding (UTF-8, quoted-printable, etc.) works flawlessly. And if there's only an HTML email, it has to strip out any scripts or styles and extracts plain text.

Then, we'll focus on the customizable support domain with `HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN`, making sure it accurately handles emails sent to the customized address and ignores ones sent to the default address.  We have to verify the staff replies, and customer replies to those, work as they should.

Following that, we'll investigate recipient discovery, which is key. We'll test `To`, `Cc`, `Bcc` scenarios with case-insensitivity to ensure correct parsing and ticket creation.  We will ensure correct handling for multiple businesses, cancelled businesses, unknown addresses, and multi-tenancy scenarios.

We will focus on the staff public reply to outbound email to customer email reply lifecycle. We need to verify that private notes or status updates without comments don't generate any emails. We'll confirm the correct generation of private reply addresses for public replies to email-origin tickets, the handling of the `In-Reply-To` and `References` headers, and that customer replies to those private addresses are properly handled. We have to ensure that a customer reply to the ticket's private reply address reopens a 'solved' or 'pending' ticket. Replies to "Reply-All" should append to the existing ticket. New messages to the plain support address should always open a new ticket, even if the subject and `In-Reply-To` headers look similar to an existing ticket. Finally, different email-origin tickets for the same customer have different reply addresses.

We will verify all authorization and security aspects on replies to emails. Non-requesters sending email to private reply addresses must be ignored. Invalid or tampered reply tokens must also be ignored. We must test that cross-tenant tokens are not allowed, along with scenarios where there are two different ticket tokens in the recipients. We'll verify that suspended customers and email from pending staff invitations are ignored.

We have to make sure that identical deliveries (same raw bytes and same `Message-ID`) are de-duplicated, as well as deliveries that have different raw bytes (e.g. extra headers, modified body) but the same `Message-ID`. **Ruthless Adversarial Audit: My Thinking Process**

Okay, so the initial run went well, *very* well in fact. But we're not stopping there. This feels great, but let's put on our adversarial hats and really try to break this thing. We need to think like a malicious actor, a QA specialist looking for every tiny flaw.

First, let's go hardcore with real-world integration tests. A live Puma server running in `test` mode, simulating HTTP requests with `curl`, right down to the `RAILS_ENV`. I want to verify that the email processing, ticket creation, and staff interaction all work *simultaneously* under load. Zero errors. Zero race conditions. Also, make sure eager loading works on a production setup.

Next up, `Message-ID` deduplication. We need to be absolutely certain it works *across* different business contexts. What happens with identical `Message-ID`s? Multi-business emails? That external sender scenario is particularly tricky. We need to make sure we're correctly deduping, and most importantly, not blocking valid retries because of an invalid one. That's the key.

Now, let's get into the nitty-gritty. `Message-ID` normalization. Angle brackets, whitespace, case sensitivity – we have to account for every single possible variation. We need to ensure that regardless of formatting, or if there's no `Message-ID` at all, we handle deduplication correctly, especially with invalid or bounced deliveries. This is critical. What about the case where an account is cancelled then reactivated? We need to verify that we're properly resetting to `:pending` and retrying.

Blank subjects. Okay, here's where we need to be extra careful. The prompt says that we're to open a ticket with a subject, but the subject is optional. That means we should create a ticket with a "fallback" subject, not reject it. Remember, in email, the subject is optional, and lots of helpdesk tickets are created with blank subjects. The correct behavior here is to provide a fallback title. We are following the prompt verbatim, and this also means we can keep things consistent with rejecting missing `From`, missing or blank body, multiple businesses, etc.

Now, let's examine the `From:` header, especially when it has multiple addresses. Technically, RFC allows multiple addresses, but practically, we almost always have one. We also need to check for invalid email formats. We need to ensure that the code handles multiple addresses and unparseable headers gracefully, returning `nil` and being rejected.

cd /app && cat <<'EOF' > app/services/inbound_email_filter.rb
class InboundEmailFilter
  AUTOMATED_PRECEDENCE = %w[bulk junk list auto_reply auto-reply autoreply].freeze

  LIST_AND_LOOP_HEADERS = %w[
    list-id
    x-list-id
    list-unsubscribe
    list-post
    list-subscribe
    list-help
    list-owner
    list-archive
    mailing-list
    x-mailing-list
    x-beenthere
    x-loop
  ].freeze

  AUTO_REPLY_HEADERS = %w[
    x-autoreply
    x-autorespond
    x-auto-reply
    x-auto-response
  ].freeze

  AUTOMATED_SENDER_LOCALS = %w[
    mailer-daemon
    postmaster
    noreply
    no-reply
    donotreply
    do-not-reply
    bounce
    bounces
    autoreply
    auto-reply
    autoresponder
  ].freeze

  def initialize(mail:, from_email: nil)
    @mail = mail
    @from_email = from_email
  end

  def ignore?
    auto_submitted? ||
      automated_precedence? ||
      list_or_loop_header? ||
      auto_reply_header? ||
      auto_response_suppress? ||
      failed_recipients_header? ||
      null_return_path? ||
      multipart_report? ||
      automated_sender?
  end

  private

  def auto_submitted?
    header_values("auto-submitted").any? do |value|
      primary = value.split(";").first.to_s.strip.downcase
      primary.present? && primary != "no"
    end
  end

  def automated_precedence?
    (header_values("precedence") + header_values("x-precedence")).any? do |value|
      AUTOMATED_PRECEDENCE.include?(value.downcase)
    end
  end

  def list_or_loop_header?
    LIST_AND_LOOP_HEADERS.any? do |name|
      header_values(name).any?(&:present?)
    end
  end

  def auto_reply_header?
    AUTO_REPLY_HEADERS.any? do |name|
      header_values(name).any? do |value|
        normalized = value.downcase
        normalized.present? && !%w[no false 0].include?(normalized)
      end
    end
  end

  def auto_response_suppress?
    header_values("x-auto-response-suppress").any? do |value|
      tokens = value.downcase.split(/[,\s]+/).reject(&:empty?)
      (tokens & %w[all oof autoreply dr rn nrn]).any?
    end
  end

  def failed_recipients_header?
    header_values("x-failed-recipients").any?(&:present?)
  end

  def null_return_path?
    fields = Array(@mail[:return_path])
    return false if fields.empty?

    fields.any? do |field|
      field.value.to_s.delete("<>").strip.empty?
    end
  rescue StandardError
    false
  end

  def multipart_report?
    return true if @mail.mime_type.to_s.downcase == "multipart/report"

    @mail.all_parts.any? do |part|
      mime = part.mime_type.to_s.downcase
      mime == "message/delivery-status" || mime == "message/disposition-notification"
    end
  rescue StandardError
    false
  end

  def automated_sender?
    return false if @from_email.blank?

    local, domain = @from_email.split("@", 2)
    return false if local.blank? || domain.blank?
    return true if domain == HelpdeskConfig.support_domain

    base_local = local.split("+", 2).first
    AUTOMATED_SENDER_LOCALS.include?(base_local)
  end

  def header_values(name)
    Array(@mail.header[name]).map { |field| field.value.to_s.strip }
  rescue StandardError
    []
  end
end
EOF

**Expanding Test Coverage for Robustness**

Okay, let's bolster our testing suite. I'm thinking we need to add a few more focused tests. Specifically, I'll beef up `test/models/ticket_test.rb` and add a new mailbox unit test at `test/mailboxes/support_mailbox_test.rb` using `ActionMailbox::TestCase`. The goal here is to make sure we're fully covering both the Action Mailbox helpers (`receive_inbound_email_from_mail` and `receive_inbound_email_from_source`) *and* the full HTTP relay ingress. We need comprehensive validation.

I've also got some edge cases in mind that are critical to address. Here's what I want to verify:

1.  **Customer Portal Replies After Email Creation:** We have to confirm that after a customer opens a ticket via email, verifies their account, *then* replies through the portal (`PATCH /api/v1/requests/:id`), that `TicketUpdater` does *not* send another email. `@mode == :customer` should prevent that. We need an explicit assertion in the test to ensure this is working correctly.

2.  **Staff Multiple Replies:** We need to test the scenario where staff replies to an email-originated ticket multiple times. We need to make sure the customer gets the expected two emails with the *same* private reply address and that the `References` header grows as the thread progresses.

3.  **Malformed/Invalid Email Handling:** We need to ensure that the system cleanly rejects emails with malformed or empty bodies, missing `From` headers, or invalid `From` addresses (like `From: not-an-email`). Critically, these rejections shouldn't block valid retries with the same `Message-ID`.

4.  **No `Message-ID` Header Handling:** This is a tricky one. We need to test how the system behaves if an email *lacks* a `Message-ID` header:
    *   The first valid email should create a ticket (Ticket #1).
    *   An exact duplicate (still no `Message-ID`) should be deduplicated.
    *   A *different* email (also without `Message-ID`) should create a *new* ticket (Ticket #2).

Okay, time for one last, meticulous check. I'm going to run through every single requirement, line by line, and confirm that I've nailed this implementation.

Action Mailbox is enabled. I've got `active_storage/engine` and `action_mailbox/engine` in place. The `HelpdeskConfig` is set up dynamically using `ENV["HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN"]`, and the support address generation for each account is handled. The mailboxes are correctly routing: `ApplicationMailbox` routes to `SupportMailbox`, then to `InboundEmailProcessor`. Got the support address generation for each account too, now.

I've configured the Action Mailbox relay ingress properly with `/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails` and the Basic Auth using `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD`.  And in the test environment, I've got everything set up to process mail synchronously, inline, before the request completes to avoid dealing with workers. Verified that in both integration tests and with a live test server.

The core of the ticket creation is in place.  Incoming mail creates a ticket with subject and the plain text message from the email body. I'm handling the fallback for no subject and stripping out HTML content properly.

For the business lookup, I'm inspecting all the relevant headers (`To`, `Cc`, `Bcc`, etc.), filtering for the correct domain, ignoring external recipients, and deduplicating addresses. If there are multiple businesses in a single email, I'm rejecting it.

Regarding the customer handling: I'm reusing existing customers if they're found.  New customers are created with a random password and are sent a verification email.  Crucially, receiving an email *doesn't* verify their account.

The staff reply process is working as intended. `TicketUpdater` is sending emails from public comments on email-origin tickets. Each ticket gets a unique reply address. Only the ticket requester can reply via email, and valid replies will re-open a ticket, and a new message to the general support address will open a new ticket.

I have strong deduplication in place using `Message-ID`. Duplicate deliveries are handled cleanly. Invalid deliveries won't block a later, valid retry, and the `InboundEmail` model correctly handles bounced emails and allows for retries.

And finally, I've implemented the filtering for automated or list mail using a range of headers and sender patterns: this is filtering for everything like `Auto-Submitted`, `Precedence`, `List-*` headers, `X-Autoreply`, and null `Return-Path` to prevent unwanted tickets.
